series.title: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1.x
series.subtitle: Token counting APIs, per-request backend credentials, stream idle timeout with failover, MCP hostname routing and backend selection, OpenTelemetry GenAI tracing, and HTTP CONNECT egress.

releases.overview: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1.0 is the first minor release on the stable 1.x API. Count tokens before you spend them: a vLLM-compatible /tokenize endpoint covers OpenAI-compatible, Bedrock, Vertex AI Gemini, and Anthropic-on-cloud backends, alongside native Anthropic /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens and OpenAI /v1/responses/input_tokens. Multi-tenant platforms can inject per-request upstream credentials from a trusted filter instead of sharing one static key. Streaming calls that stall on time-to-first-token now fail over to the next backend via streamIdleTimeout. MCP routes pick up hostname scoping and CEL-based backend selection so a shared MCP gateway can isolate tenants. Observability grows with optional OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, an importable Grafana dashboard, and JSON logs. Locked-down networks can send all upstream AI traffic through an HTTP CONNECT forward proxy.

items.title: vLLM-compatible /tokenize across providers
items.description: Count tokens for a prompt without generating a completion. Chat messages and completion prompts are accepted in the vLLM tokenize request shape, so cost estimation and context-window checks work the same way against vLLM, GCP Vertex AI Gemini, GCP Anthropic, AWS Bedrock Converse, and AWS Anthropic. Translated backends return {"count": N}; native vLLM backends may also return token IDs and max_model_len. OpenAI itself has no tokenize REST API — configure an OpenAI-schema backend only when the upstream (for example vLLM) actually implements /tokenize.

items.title: Anthropic /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens
items.description: Anthropic-native clients can count input tokens for a Messages request — including system prompts and tools — without creating a message. Routed to Anthropic, GCP Anthropic, and AWS Anthropic backends, so Claude clients estimate cost and validate request size through the same gateway path they already use for inference.

items.title: OpenAI /v1/responses/input_tokens
items.description: The Responses API counterpart of count-tokens: send the same body as /v1/responses and get back an input token count. Works with OpenAI and Azure OpenAI (with automatic api-version injection), so agentic and multimodal Responses workloads can check context-window fit before paying for a generation.

items.title: Anthropic-format /anthropic/v1/models
items.description: Claude clients that call Anthropic's model list endpoint now get the gateway's configured catalog in Anthropic's response shape, scoped by hostname the same way /v1/models is. Anthropic SDKs can discover available models without speaking OpenAI's list format.

items.title: Per-request upstream credentials via credentialOverride
items.description: A trusted filter (ext_authz or a preceding ext_proc) can now supply the backend credential per request instead of every caller sharing one static key in BackendSecurityPolicy. Source the credential from Envoy dynamic metadata (preferred — clients cannot forge it) or from a request header that the gateway strips before the backend sees it. Missing credentials fall back to the configured secret by default, or return 401 when fallbackToConfigured is false. API keys, Anthropic, Azure, GCP, and AWS SigV4 are all supported.

items.title: Per-request AWS SigV4 credentials
items.description: AWSCredentials overrides carry the three-part SigV4 input — access key, secret, and optional session token — rather than a single string. Header source uses the x-aigw-aws- prefix (or a custom prefix such as x-aws-); metadata source reads a struct with fixed accessKeyId / secretAccessKey / sessionToken fields. A partial credential fails the request instead of silently falling back, so a misconfigured injector cannot send unsigned traffic. Prefer metadata over headers: a secret access key on the wire is a worse leak than an API key.

items.title: HTTP CONNECT forward proxy for upstream AI traffic
items.description: GatewayConfig.spec.forwardProxy tunnels every upstream LLM connection from Gateways that reference the config through an HTTP CONNECT proxy. Intended for data planes in locked-down networks that cannot reach providers directly. The address is host:port (hostname or IP; port required). Envoy's http_11_proxy transport socket preserves the upstream TLS session, so provider certificates still terminate at OpenAI, Bedrock, or Vertex — not at the proxy.

items.title: Correct SigV4 signing for Bedrock VPC endpoints
items.description: Bedrock requests through PrivateLink or a custom internal hostname now sign over the actual upstream host resolved at config time, not the downstream gateway authority. Region is derived from the Bedrock host when it encodes one, so a VPCE in a different region than the configured BackendSecurityPolicy still produces a valid signature instead of a silent 403.

items.title: Stream idle timeout with failover to the next backend
items.description: AIGatewayRouteRule.streamIdleTimeout bounds how long Envoy waits without receiving any upstream bytes on a streaming response. If the timer fires before the first token, Envoy resets the stream and a retry policy can fail over to the next backend in the rule — so a hung model no longer burns the full timeouts.request budget. If it fires mid-stream after bytes have already reached the client, the stream is cut with a 504. Pair it with a BackendTrafficPolicy whose retry covers reset; without retry, the idle timeout still fails fast but does not fail over.

items.title: Hostname-based routing on MCPRoute
items.description: MCPRoute.spec.hostnames scopes an MCP endpoint to specific hosts, the same way AIGatewayRoute.spec.hostnames scopes LLM traffic. The generated HTTPRoute lands in the per-host virtual host instead of the wildcard vhost, so team-a.mcp.example.com and team-b.mcp.example.com can expose different MCP server sets from a single Gateway.

items.title: Per-request MCP backend selection
items.description: MCPRoute.spec.backendSelector restricts which of a route's backends a given client session fans out to. CEL rules are evaluated once per candidate backend at session initialize — not on every tools/call — so a large shared MCPRoute no longer contacts backends the caller is not entitled to. Default action is Deny; if no backend is allowed, initialize returns 403 rather than a 500. Expressions can match JWT claims or a trusted header such as x-ai-eg-mcp-backend-subset.

items.title: Merged backend capabilities and shared Backends
items.description: Initialize now advertises capability extensions declared by the backends themselves, so clients see the union of what the aggregated servers actually support. The controller also shares one Envoy Gateway Backend per namespace instead of creating one per MCPRoute, cutting duplicate cluster config when many routes point at the same MCP servers.

items.title: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
items.description: Set AI_GATEWAY_TRACING_SEMCONV=gen_ai on the ext-proc to emit gen_ai.* span attributes instead of OpenInference. OpenTelemetry-native backends can then consume traces without an OpenInference translator. Message content is opt-in via OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT. The same flag switches MCP spans from gateway-specific mcp.* attributes to the OpenTelemetry MCP conventions. An unrecognized value fails startup rather than silently falling back. Span names include the model, so cardinality is higher than OpenInference's fixed names — update dashboards before switching. The GenAI conventions are still marked Development upstream.

items.title: Importable Grafana dashboard for GenAI metrics
items.description: An example dashboard covering the gen_ai_* Prometheus metrics ships in examples/monitoring/grafana-dashboard.json. Panels include token usage by type (input, output, cached, cache-creation, reasoning), P50/P95/P99 request duration, time-to-first-token vs inter-token latency, original-vs-response model mismatch, QPS, token burn rate, and per-model success rate — so you can import a working view of gateway traffic instead of building PromQL from scratch.

items.title: MCP resource URI in access logs and JSON controller logs
items.description: Resource reads now populate mcp_resource_uri in the io.envoy.ai_gateway dynamic metadata, so access logs can record which MCP resource was fetched. Controller and ext-proc logs accept --logFormat=json (Helm: controller.logFormat / extProc.logFormat) for pipelines such as Loki, Datadog, or Cloud Logging. MCP requests also honour inbound W3C traceparent, so an agent trace continues through the MCP gateway instead of starting a disconnected span.

items.title: Structured output for Claude on GCP Vertex AI
items.description: JSON-schema constrained decoding now works for Claude models on Vertex AI that advertise output_config (including Claude 4.5, Opus 4.6+, Sonnet 5, and Mythos/Fable). This closes the gap left in v0.6, when Anthropic and AWS Bedrock Claude already supported structured output but GCP did not. Declare a response format once and get schema-shaped output from Claude regardless of whether it runs on Anthropic, Bedrock, or GCP — unsupported models skip the constraint rather than failing the request.

items.title: OpenAI reasoning_effort forwarded to Bedrock as reasoning_config
items.description: Clients that set reasoning_effort on chat completions now have that value forwarded to AWS Bedrock as additionalModelRequestFields.reasoning_config. Models such as Amazon Nova and GLM that read Bedrock's reasoning_config knob pick up the same effort the OpenAI client already sends, without a Bedrock-specific request body.

items.title: Responses API tool_search, unknown tools, and Codex inputs
items.description: The Responses API accepts the built-in tool_search tool and additional_tools, preserves unknown tool types instead of rejecting the request, and accepts Codex-style agent input items. Newer OpenAI client features pass through the gateway instead of failing schema validation.

items.title: Controller PDB, topology spread, pod labels, and security context
items.description: The Helm chart can emit a PodDisruptionBudget (controller.podDisruptionBudget.enabled, default off), honour topologySpreadConstraints, and attach extra podLabels. Controller pods now default to a restricted security context (non-root UID 65532, all capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation). Override the values if you run a custom controller image that cannot use that UID.

items.title: Sharded ext-proc config secrets
items.description: Filter configuration is split across multiple Secrets instead of a single object, so large Gateway configs no longer fail Kubernetes' 1 MiB Secret size limit. The aigw CLI reassembles the bundle automatically. Ext-proc pods are also rolled when injected config drifts, so a stale sidecar cannot keep serving an old route table after a successful reconcile.

apiChanges.title: AIGatewayRouteRule.name
apiChanges.description: Optional unique name copied onto the generated HTTPRoute rule. Names must be unique within the route; route-not-found is reserved. Use this when you need a stable section name for status, policies, or debugging instead of an index.

apiChanges.title: AIGatewayRouteRule.streamIdleTimeout
apiChanges.description: Optional Gateway API duration. The extension server sets route.retry_policy.per_try_idle_timeout on every xDS route generated from the rule. Unset means no per-try idle timeout. Pair with timeouts.request as the overall deadline.

apiChanges.title: BackendSecurityPolicy.spec.credentialOverride (v1beta1)
apiChanges.description: Optional per-request credential source. Exactly one of fromRequestHeaders or fromDynamicMetadata must be set. Header defaults are x-aigw-api-key, x-aigw-anthropic-api-key, x-aigw-azure-api-key, x-aigw-azure-access-token, x-aigw-gcp-access-token, and the x-aigw-aws- prefix for SigV4. Metadata requires namespace; key defaults to the matching x-aigw-* name (or x-aigw-aws-credentials for AWS). fallbackToConfigured defaults to true.

apiChanges.title: GatewayConfig.spec.forwardProxy
apiChanges.description: Optional HTTP CONNECT proxy for all upstream AI traffic from Gateways that reference this config. address is required and must be host:port.

apiChanges.title: MCPRoute.spec.hostnames
apiChanges.description: Optional list of hostnames (max 16) matched against the HTTP Host header. When set, the generated HTTPRoute includes them so the MCP route is scoped to the per-host virtual host.

apiChanges.title: MCPRoute.spec.backendSelector
apiChanges.description: Optional CEL-based selector evaluated once per candidate backend at session initialize. defaultAction defaults to Deny. Each rule has an optional cel expression (max 4096 characters) and action (default Allow). Max 32 rules. request.mcp.method, request.mcp.tool, and request.mcp.params are not populated at selection time.

bugFixes.title: Stale Content-Encoding on translated error responses
bugFixes.description: Translated error bodies no longer keep the upstream Content-Encoding header. Clients no longer fail to decode an uncompressed error payload that still claimed to be gzip or brotli.

bugFixes.title: Anthropic ping events keep streams alive
bugFixes.description: Anthropic ping SSE events now emit an empty chunk on translated paths, so intermediaries and clients that time out on silence no longer drop a healthy Claude stream.

bugFixes.title: Gateway local replies are not reprocessed as upstream responses
bugFixes.description: Ext-proc no longer treats Envoy local replies (rate-limit, timeout, auth) as provider payloads. Local error bodies pass through instead of being force-translated into a malformed LLM response.

bugFixes.title: Anthropic cache_control on the Bedrock path
bugFixes.description: Prompt-caching cache_control markers now translate onto AWS Bedrock, including tool-result cache control and Bedrock tool cache points as their own tools[] element. Cached prefixes that previously silently dropped now actually hit Bedrock's cache.

bugFixes.title: Bedrock reasoning_content serialized as a plain string
bugFixes.description: Non-streaming and streaming Bedrock reasoning content is emitted as a plain string, with signatures carried via thinking_blocks. Clients that expected a string and previously received an object no longer fail to parse Claude-on-Bedrock reasoning.

bugFixes.title: Unsupported Anthropic tool types error instead of dropping
bugFixes.description: Unknown Anthropic tool types now fail the request rather than being silently stripped. You get a clear error instead of a tool-less prompt that looks like it succeeded.

bugFixes.title: Cross-namespace InferencePool backendRef honours namespace
bugFixes.description: An InferencePool referenced from another namespace is now resolved in that namespace instead of the route's. Cross-namespace inference pools that previously 404'd at reconcile now work when the ReferenceGrant allows them.

bugFixes.title: Anthropic streaming cache tokens no longer double-counted
bugFixes.description: Input and cache token counts on Anthropic message_delta events are merged once, including on the OpenAI→Anthropic streaming path. Usage metrics and access logs no longer inflate cached-token cost on streaming Claude calls.

bugFixes.title: Credential leak in Envoy ext-proc debug logs
bugFixes.description: Envoy HTTP and ext-proc debug logging is capped, and credential header mutations are always redacted in debug output. Passthrough endpoints also redact user content. Debug-level logging is no longer a credential-exfiltration path.

bugFixes.title: Gemini streaming tool-call finish reasons and reasoning tokens
bugFixes.description: Newer Gemini models such as gemini-3.5-flash now map streaming tool-call finish reasons correctly, and reasoning tokens are counted in streaming metrics. Streaming Gemini tool use no longer reports a wrong finish reason or drops thinking-token usage.

breakingChanges.title: Helm controller security context defaults
breakingChanges.description: The Helm chart now sets a restricted podSecurityContext and container securityContext on the controller (non-root UID/GID 65532, all capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation, RuntimeDefault seccomp). Previously both were empty. If you run a custom controller image that cannot use UID 65532, override controller.podSecurityContext and controller.securityContext in your values. PodDisruptionBudget remains off unless you set controller.podDisruptionBudget.enabled: true.
